A protein design competition co-sponsored with Adaptyv Bio offers up to $1 million in Claude credits and highlights these advancements.

Brown was a foundational contributor to the development of reasoning models. It uses ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling, for 1.76 effective bits per weight and a total model footprint of 5.9GB. The model supports a 262K-token context window and multimodal text-and-image input. It can be run on Nvidia GPUs via CUDA and on Apple devices via MLX through custom low-bit kernels.

articles.headline: Natural General Intelligence

AI promises abundance via the automation of knowledge work, but the Earth system is already fully automated. Natural General Intelligence is a foundation model grounded in the state and dynamics of the planet itself. This article explains the concept, shows readers how it can be built, and explains why it is necessary.

Huawei's chip-making technology still trails Nvidia's, but the company is developing workarounds and new designs to squeeze in more computing power while using less advanced equipment.

The company is trying to create a framework to track agents and monitor the amount of work they do.

articles.headline: How SpaceX Streamlined the Raptor Engine
articles.blurb: The differences between the versions of the Raptor rocket engine are stark. Many people initially didn't believe SpaceX when the company released a picture of the three generations of the design. The streamlining of the design also brought meaningful gains in performance - the Raptor 3 provides about 35% more thrust than the Raptor 1. This article looks at what specifically SpaceX changed that allowed it to take the Raptor from a tangle of wires and pipes into the svelte, streamlined engine it is today.

articles.headline: Helix 2.5: Zero-Shot 30-Home Generalization
articles.blurb: Helix 2.5 is an advanced neural network pretrained on Index, Figure's global-scale dataset of human behavior. It can tidy living rooms, fold towels, and make beds in homes it has never seen. The model is the first evidence that whole-body intelligence can be learned from human experience and transferred to new scenarios. Index is now generating roughly 35 minutes of new human experience every second - if Helix 2.5 is any guide, more data and compute should translate directly into more of the physical world learned before a robot ever enters a new home.

articles.headline: Hacking OpenAI
articles.blurb: Researchers chained two critical vulnerabilities to compromise multiple OpenAI employees' ChatGPT accounts in July. The accounts could access internal OpenAI repositories and potentially many other connectors. They used one employee's Codex to open a PR in OpenAI's internal monorepo. This post provides a full timeline of the disclosure process and details about how the vulnerabilities were discovered.

articles.headline: WebKit Features for Safari 27.0
articles.blurb: The release notes on the WebKit features for Safari 27.0 are the longest yet, detailing 83 features, including Safari MCP. Safari MCP makes working with coding agents dramatically easier. It gives users' agent of choice control over the browser window so it can see how code renders. The MCP provides access to the DOM, network requests, screenshots, and console output, allowing agents to do more with less effort from users.

articles.headline: Inside the White House Tussle to Sway Trump on AI
articles.blurb: Anthropic's Mythos model sparked a shift within the White House as officials started realizing that AI can be used to launch cyberattacks and pose national-security threats. White House officials and AI executives are working on regulatory efforts, but when they disagree, the executives have gone directly to Trump. Trump has remained resolute that the nation needs to accelerate AI development and continue to build the data centers that are powering the AI boom.

articles.headline: The Startup That Built OpenAI's Biggest Data Center Is Now Making Tiny Ones

It is manufacturing them in factories, loading them onto flatbed trucks, and deploying them wherever it can find available power. The company believes this is a faster and cheaper method than solely relying on large construction projects. Giant clusters with hundreds of thousands of chips are useful for training, but inference can be done with considerably smaller amounts of chips.

A validated fix was deployed fleetwide, but some instances required manual restarts and continued experiencing scheduled-job failures.

articles.blurb: Harness demonstrates a three-stage CI/CD pipeline that uses Terraform to dynamically provision a unique Docker virtual registry and Docker Hub upstream proxy, builds and pushes an image, then deploys it to Kubernetes with rolling updates and automatic rollback. Output variables and Harness expressions connect resources across stages without hardcoding.

articles.headline: I don't like LLMs
articles.blurb: LLMs can be highly useful while still being unpleasant to interact with because they present fabricated and correct information with the same confident, human-like tone. AI agents also reflect the values and culture of the companies that build them, making trust, behavior, and interaction design important alongside raw model capability.

articles.headline: Running OpenBao on Kubernetes with a CloudNativePG PostgreSQL backend
articles.blurb: OpenBao and CloudNativePG can manage infrastructure secrets on Kubernetes without vendor lock-in by using certificate authentication and synchronous replication. OpenBao uses the CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster as an encrypted key-value store, and a schema-init job revokes default public permissions to lock down the database. CloudNativePG automatically renews client certificates every 90 days, but OpenBao requires a rolling restart to load the new files. The setup runs three OpenBao replicas and three Postgres instances across separate nodes.

articles.headline: Browserskill (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: BrowserSkill connects AI agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex to a user's logged-in browser. The tool requires agents to explicitly borrow open tabs and return them after finishing a task. It includes a command-line interface, a daemon, and a browser extension.

articles.headline: Cline (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Cline is an open-source coding agent that runs in IDEs, terminals, and as a native desktop app for macOS and Windows. It reads project structures, edits files, and executes terminal commands with human-in-the-loop approval. Users can switch between Plan and Act modes or use the SDK to build custom tools and coordinate multi-agent teams. The tool runs on any model and supports integrations through plugins or MCP servers.

articles.headline: Komodor Extends AI SRE Reach for Kubernetes to AI Agents

The platform aims to help teams manage growing fleets of production AI agents while preserving existing change management and governance practices.

articles.headline: Getting started with runtime security and Falco
articles.blurb: Runtime security protects cloud workloads while they are executing, filling gaps that posture management cannot catch, such as zero-days, privilege escalation, and compromised credentials. Falco provides cloud-native runtime detection across hosts, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud services by analyzing system calls and plugin events, adding contextual alerts, and deploying easily with Helm.

articles.headline: HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents?
articles.blurb: Coding-agent harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Pi can produce similar task success rates while using dramatically different amounts of tokens and money. Across 21 model–harness combinations on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0, harness choice changed cost by as much as 5×, and the model provider's own harness was not consistently the most efficient option.

Users can test furniture, decor, paint colors, and lighting, remove or swap individual objects, or try a completely different style. Launching in beta in the US and Canada, Restyle brings Pinterest Intelligence directly into the consumer experience, helping people compare options and turn inspiration into more concrete plans for their homes.

These tools support repeatable image and vector generation at scale, and people can browse the Community to see tools others have built. While any output type, including video and 3D renderings, can be published to the Community, only image and vector generation tools work within Figma Design itself.

articles.headline: Samsung starts rolling out Android 17 with One UI 9, confirms initial list of Galaxy devices
articles.blurb: Samsung has officially begun rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after a four-month beta. The update introduces new Galaxy AI features, including My FanCam, Creative Studio, Now Brief enhancements, improved privacy and security tools, and easier access to warranty information. Samsung says the update will gradually expand to more Galaxy phones and tablets, including recent S-series, Fold, Flip, and Tab models.

articles.headline: The Invisible Side of Design Engineering
articles.blurb: Design engineering has no fixed definition, and social media makes it look like little more than building animated eye-candy components. Day-to-day work leans heavily on invisible priorities like accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and the edge cases only real users surface. A great experience often comes down to unglamorous effort, like spending an afternoon on an accessibility fix or making a landing page load slightly faster.

articles.headline: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era
articles.blurb: User experience design has evolved through five major eras—from Human Factors and the Web to Mobile, Design Systems, and AI—each contributing a lasting lesson while leaving behind habits that later became limitations. Designers should focus less on producing interfaces and more on shaping systems, information architecture, constraints, and the rules that govern intelligent experiences, as these are becoming the most valuable skills in the AI era. Rather than replacing UX, AI continues the historical pattern of making creation cheaper while shifting designers' value toward higher-level thinking and decision-making.

articles.headline: Seven lines of client feedback that knock you sideways, and how to stop them living rent-free in your head
articles.blurb: Clients often give confusing or unhelpful feedback because of uncertainty, internal politics, or a lack of design knowledge rather than problems with the work itself. Common situations include vague requests like “make it look less designed,” Canva comparisons, hidden budgets, feedback by committee, and indecisive comments such as “I'll know it when I see it.” Responding with calm questions, clarifying underlying concerns, setting expectations early, and guiding clients through the design process can turn frustrating feedback into more productive conversations.

articles.blurb: Current agent-planning interfaces trap people in walls of Markdown text, even though humans read roughly 240 words a minute against an agent's 4,500. Chuukese wayfinding and Susan Leigh Star's boundary-object theory frame a case for thicker, visual, interactive, and social interfaces instead of thin text exchanges. A GitHub Next prototype called Chopin explores multiplayer, real-time planning where coworkers and agents share visual, editable plans rather than solitary text approvals.

articles.headline: Why Canva hit the brakes on its huge AI rollout (and what other brands can learn from it)
articles.blurb: Canva revealed that overwhelming demand for Canva AI 2.0 forced it to pause the rollout, leading the company to re-engineer the platform and reduce AI processing costs by nearly 90% while making it five times faster. Rather than relying on a single AI model, Canva is investing in a diverse AI strategy focused on delivering reliable, affordable, and user-friendly experiences that can adapt as AI technology evolves.

articles.headline: Fitts's Law: Why the Easy Button Wins
articles.blurb: Fitts's Law, developed from 1954 cockpit-control research, holds that reaching a target gets faster as it grows larger and slower as it sits farther away. Screen edges and corners act as "magic pixels" that are effectively infinite in size on desktop, while touchscreens replace that trick with a thumb-reachable zone. The same principle for making desired actions easy to click can be inverted into dark patterns, like oversized subscribe buttons next to tiny cancel links.

articles.headline: Artist Turns Renaissance Paintings, Digital Fragments, and Dream Logic into Surreal Worlds That Feel More Like Memories Than Collages

Creator-led collaborations delivered the strongest results, with smaller brands seeing 5X more interactions than non-collab posts. In ecommerce and retail, accepted collabs generated more than 5X the shares and reposts of standard posts. Reels saw the biggest engagement gains.

articles.headline: Do ChatGPT & Google AI Get Your Business Details Right?
articles.blurb: AI search often gives inaccurate business information, especially when a company leaves key details vague or unpublished. In a study of 600 businesses, 27% of Google AI Overview answers and 20% of ChatGPT answers included details the business did not publish. Google AI Overviews got 84% of answers right when businesses published clearly, compared with 63% when information was vague or missing. AI systems often fill gaps from third-party directories, so you should audit those listings and keep website copy, Google Business Profiles, and structured data consistent. Agencies can turn this into a quick audit by checking how Google and ChatGPT describe each client and correcting the sources behind inaccurate answers.

articles.headline: Competitor Email Monitoring: What to Track and How to Do It
articles.blurb: Competitor email monitoring helps brands spot patterns in how others approach email. Start by tracking 5-8 direct competitors each month and compare their send frequency and offer rates. Read their subject lines to see how they frame promotions and other messages. Open unusual emails and note what stands out or changes over time. Use those findings to identify gaps and choose one idea to test, rather than copying a competitor's strategy.

articles.headline: The Amazon CRO playbook: How to optimize your listings and beat your competitors
articles.blurb: Amazon CRO works best as a research and testing process rather than a series of listing tweaks. Start by finding funnel problems in Seller Central, then use customer feedback, reviews, and user testing to identify specific objections and turn them into targeted listing changes. Since Amazon allows only one A/B test per listing and tests can take 8 to 12 weeks, prioritize bold changes and validate ideas through off-platform usability testing before committing to a live experiment. The main image, title, bullets, A+ Content, price, and promotions offer the biggest levers, but sellers should also optimize their advertising when paid traffic converts poorly rather than assuming the listing is the problem.

articles.headline: How To Create A Product Launch People Talk About
articles.blurb: A product launch only generates lasting attention when it gives people something to do beyond scroll past it, whether that is showing up somewhere in person, guessing what is coming, or filming something unusual enough to send to a friend. The brands getting the most mileage out of a launch treat it as an ongoing event instead of a single announcement, letting creators and customers do the distribution for free. None of it requires a bigger budget, just a reason for people to keep talking after day one.

articles.headline: Pinterest unveils Visual Search Ads, bringing new performance advertising to visual discovery
articles.blurb: Pinterest is turning visual search into a lower-funnel advertising channel through Visual Search Ads, which place sponsored products in search results and Pin closeups as users compare options and approach a purchase decision. More than half of Pinterest's 80 billion monthly searches are commercial, giving advertisers a large pool of users who already show buying intent. It is also adding Priority Products and self-serve A/B testing to give advertisers more control over automated campaigns.

articles.headline: Custom GPT retirement and migration FAQ

Migration will turn GPT instructions into a plugin skill and connected apps into apps, but custom actions will need to be rebuilt separately. Migrated GPTs become read-only, and users should test the replacement before switching. Plugin access and sharing will depend on account and workspace permissions.

articles.headline: FBI Probes Service Selling 153M+ Drivers Licenses

Based on interviews with individuals whose licenses are available for purchase on this service, it appears to be siphoning images collected by a widely-used identity verification company based in Louisiana. KrebsOnSecurity also has learned that the New Orleans field office of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) today launched an official inquiry into the source of the images.

articles.headline: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
articles.blurb: Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever. In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses." The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

articles.headline: Who’s Tracking You? Use This New Service to Find Out
articles.blurb: It can be daunting to determine who's responsible for showing ads on the websites we visit, or who's harvesting data from the mobile apps we use every day. That information is already semi-public, but it is not easily parsed and traditionally much of it has remained walled away in the hands of large advertising platforms. Not anymore: A powerful and free new service called DecryptAds scrapes and correlates this adtech data and makes it simple to quickly learn a great deal about the entities that are tracking you.

articles.blurb: Group trapped at Hotel Bamy after US removal as rights groups sound alarm over poor conditions and violence Two men that the Trump administration expelled to Equatorial Guinea were bound, fitted with bags over their heads, beaten and pushed down a flight of stairs, all in plain view of other US deportees, according to witnesses and human rights lawyers. The men – one from Egypt and one from Eritrea – were then taken to a prison. About 30 detainees from the US remain trapped at a hotel in the outskirts of the coastal city of Malabo after being deported from the US. Detainees have said they believe the men were beaten for telling the press and human rights advocates about the poor conditions and violence inside the hotel, and that they are haunted by flashbacks and terrified they will be retaliated against next.

The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.

Firefighters investigating a report of a minor fire at a home in the suburban New Orleans community of Marrero on Tuesday spotted the cat in question – an African serval – behind the residence in a chain-linked enclosure resembling a cramped baseball batting cage, a spokesperson for the local animal protection services said.

articles.blurb: More than 180 writers sign letter renewing calls for information on 12 authors detained incommunicado since 2001 crackdown on free speech by Isaias Afwerki More than 180 writers have signed a letter to Eritrean president Isaias Afwerki calling for proof of life for 12 writers arrested in 2001. Nobel laureates Olga Tokarczuk and JM Coetzee join prominent writers including Colm Tóibín, Elif Shafak, Isabel Allende, Ben Okri, Yann Martel, Kamila Shamsie and Tsitsi Dangarembga in signing the letter organised by PEN International and dated 18 September, marking 25 years since a government crackdown on the independent press. “Within days, Eritrea’s free press and the nation’s independent voices were systematically crushed,” opens the letter.

articles.headline: New cat species identified for first time in more than a century in Bolivia
articles.blurb: New species of wild feline was discovered in Bolivia’s Yungas forest that is smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat A diminutive wild cat that inhabits Bolivia’s ⁠cloud forest has been identified as a previously unknown species, marking the first time a new living feline species has been formally named and described in more than a century. The cat, called tilcayo by local communities, is part of a group called tiger ⁠cats found across much of South ⁠America. It was found in Bolivia’s ​lush Yungas forest, a mountainous region where forests are often covered by clouds and surrounded by high humidity, according to researchers. It measures about 18in (46cm) long and weighs about 3lb (1.4kg), making it smaller than the average domestic ⁠cat.

articles.headline: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.blurb: Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”
